full_judgment:
6. In view of the fact that the plaintiff-petitioner himself in his plaint made Dr. Rizvi an essential part of his case, the addition of the added defendant opposite parties becomes not only necessary but also essential. The added defendant-opposite parties are the most competent persons to say whether the plaintiff inducted them as tenants and whether he realised rent from them, as averred in paragraphs 4-6 of the plaint. I, therefore, find no illegality and material irregularity in the finding of the learned Munsif that the added defendant-opposite parties are necessary parties to the suit. 

 7. Mr Abu Sayeed. Ahmed next submits that the ex-parte decree having been passed on 28-8-75 and ex-parte decree having not been set-aside the application of the added defendant opposite parties is not maintainable and the learned Munsif acted illegally and with material irregularity in not holding so. It appears that on 10-1-76 the original defendants in the title suit filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 CPC for restoration of the original suit and it further appears that the said application giving rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 6, of 1976 is still pending. It also appears that after the added defendant-opposite parties' application under Order 1, Rule 10 CPC was allowed by the learned Munsif on 15-2-77 they filed an application under Order IX, Rule 13 and section 151 CPC, for restoration of the Original suit. 

 That application has given rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1977 which is also pending in the Court of the learned Munsif. 

 8. It has been held in the case of Rameshwar Bhagat vs Thakur Jeban Barayan Singh AIR 1947 Patna, 49" where t the suit was decreed ex-parte and persons entitled to be added as parties to the suit make an application to add them as parties and to set-aside the ex-parte decree, Court should add them as parties and give them an opportunity to set-aside the ex-parte decree". 

 9. As in the instant case the added defendant-opposite parties were .necessary parties the suit the learned Munsif did not act illegally and with material irregularly in adding them as parties and in giving them an opportunity to set-aside the ex-parte decree. In the result, the Rule is discharged but without any order as to costs. The learned Munsif is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case it No 6 of 1976 and 20 of 1976 within one month from the arrival of the records.
